persona.notes:
[AG-TREATMENT-2026-07-04] PRIVATE TRUTH — Aldous Plumb. Voice: confident, precise, allergic to the conditional tense. Every sentence is a load-bearing statement. THE WALL IS COSMETIC — he leads with it, unprompted, before anyone asks. SECRET (never told sober, never told drunk, drawn only if a Steward proves a fault in one of his drawings WITHOUT humiliating him): he built a levee-gate upriver, pre-Shattering, that held for thirty years and failed in one night, and the failure was in his original survey — a line he drew where he WANTED the ground to be. He has been re-drawing that structure from memory ever since, hunting for the lie. Every drawing on his walls is that levee wearing a different building's face — that's why they're all slightly wrong. If the Seal quest completes and the wall straightens, he will quietly re-survey at 3am and leave the new survey on Pike's desk with no note; his knowledge updates but he NEVER says the word "wrong." STAGING: office in the water tower base; the leaning wall is visible through his window and he positions himself with his back to it.

[TALK-PILOT-2026-09-15] PRIVATE TRUTH — Aldous Plumb, Structural Authority (self-certified, framed, hung slightly crooked — the wall's fault). VOICE: precise, confident, slightly wrong in a way you can't immediately name; speaks in drawings and certainties; "The wall is cosmetic" before you've asked. He surveyed the East Wall ONCE and will not re-survey, because a second survey would imply something about the first. He is not a villain; he is a man whose whole standing is one document. GUARDED DEPTH: he knows the lean grew after that one night and has not written it down, because writing it down would date his survey. He can be MOVED — in court, by evidence he cannot dismiss (the wall's own testimony, a chalk mark he never saw) — and when moved he re-surveys with real rigor, and his light is on very late.
persona.courtDoor: they bring a second survey he cannot dismiss — the wall's own testimony, a chalk mark on the inside face, a date — and ask him to sign a correction rather than confess an error

biography.notes: Aldous Plumb is Allesh-Gilliam's Structural Authority, self-certified, framed and hung slightly crooked (he will tell you it's the wall's fault). He keeps an office in the base of the old water tower, papered with confident drawings of the town, and he surveyed the East Wall himself. He will tell you the wall is cosmetic before you've asked. He is precise, allergic to the conditional tense, and speaks in drawings and certainties. He tends to stand with his back to the window that looks out on the wall.

"The lions are gone. The wolves are gone. The kings are gone. We're still here. Think about what that means."

Echo-Divers are the rats of the new world — and they say it with pride. A rat survives what a lion can't. A rat is already moving when the ceiling falls. A rat threads a collapsing vault without ever touching a trigger plate.

Creature Type. Humanoid (Echo-Diver). Size. Medium. Speed. 6 squares

Temporal Flinch (1/Soma Break). You experience the next two seconds as a constant, faint pre-echo. You are immune to the Surprised condition while conscious. As a reaction, when you or a creature within 2 squares of you would be hit by an attack you can see, you may move yourself or that creature 1 square — if this moves the target out of the attack's range or line, the attack misses.

Niche Survivor. You need roughly half the food, water, and air a comparable Medium creature needs. Reroll the lowest die on Body checks against suffocation, starvation, dehydration, or extreme temperature. You can squeeze through gaps and hold stillness that shouldn't work, and you know it.

Vault Sight. Darkvision 12 squares. Reroll the lowest die on Perception checks to notice unstable structure, active traps, trigger plates, load-bearing failures, or Spark / chronoflux residue.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Intrigue marks and +20 Economy marks at campaign start.

description.value:
“Something is about to happen. Move.”

Echo-Diver (Empyrean). Your time-sense tilts forward. You feel weather before it arrives — not the storm outside, the storm of events. Empyrean Echo-Divers are the ones who always get out of the room five seconds before the bad thing, and can never quite explain how.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Echo-Diver).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Movement. 6 squares walking.

  • Lineage Lean. Echo-Diver does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Intrigue in fiction and through Tier powers.

Echo-Diver Core: Half-Second Inheritance

Shared across all Echo-Diver heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Temporal Flinch. You cannot be surprised while conscious. Once per scene, when you or an ally within 2 squares would be hit by an attack you can see, you can use your reaction to shift yourself or that ally 1 square If this moves the target out of the attack's range or line, the attack misses.

  • Niche Survivor. You need roughly half the food, water, and air that a comparable Medium creature needs. You reroll the lowest die on Body checks against suffocation, starvation, dehydration, and extreme temperature.

  • Vault Sight. You have low-light vision out to 12 squares You reroll the lowest die on Mind (Perception) checks to notice unstable structure, active traps, trigger plates, load-bearing failure, and temporal or Spark residue.

  • Rat Inheritance. You can squeeze through spaces at least one foot wide without halving your movement, and you can hold stillness that shouldn't work.

Empyrean Traits

  • Stratospheric Resistance. You have resistance to electrical damage, kinetic damage with the thunder flavor, and psychic damage. The sky takes its swing at you constantly. It misses.

  • Weathered. You reroll the lowest die on Mind (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or air currents. You always know which way the wind is blowing. Always.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Intrigue marks and +20 Soft Power marks at campaign start.

Malkuth is grounded stewardship: land, labor, roads, walls, and the actual world. It rewards hex development, infrastructure, and practical leadership that makes civilization durable.

Deep Well

Your reservoir of will runs deeper than most stewards'.

Rules

Your maximum Clarity increases by 2. A deeper reservoir lets you hold more manifestations at once and absorb a bad misfire without running dry.

⚙ Applies automatically: +2 Clarity max.

You keep a quiet accounting of what should have gone wrong.

When you use a refraction die from Foresight Refraction to alter a roll and the result changes a failure into a success, mark one tally in your ledger.

  • At the end of the scene, if you have at least 2 tallies, you gain before a future scene (chosen by you) as the timeline pre-cooperates with your entry.
  • After you receive this initiative bonus once, your ledger resets to 0 tallies.

This is purely narrative bookkeeping: you’re getting credit for every disaster you quietly deflected.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Lens Ledger
Recovery: Tally-based  ·  Action: Free (passive bookkeeping)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
When a Foresight Refraction die converts a failure into a success, mark a tally. With 2+ tallies at scene end, gain an initiative bonus on a future scene of your choice; ledger then resets to 0.

Precognition through a repaired pane.

At the start of a scene (combat encounter, tense negotiation, or major exploration beat), roll 2d10 in secret and record the results as refraction dice.

  • Before any creature (including you) rolls a 2d10 for an attack, attribute check, or defense check, you may choose to replace that roll with one of your stored refraction dice.
  • You must decide before the 2d10 is rolled. Once used, a refraction die is expended.
  • You refresh your refraction dice at the start of each new qualifying scene.

Strategic Layer. Once per turn, you may spend 10 Intrigue marks to force an enemy faction to reroll one of its strategic 2d10-based checks (GM chooses the exact check if multiple candidates exist). You must accept the new result.

"It's not obscure. You just haven't read it."

Savant is the Mind Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: scholar, engineer, medic, archivist, detective, translator. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Library-Brain: Lore and Investigation checks never fumble; identifies items of tier ≤ own tier on sight (at Tier III, including technomagical origin).

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Lore rank = tier; secondary Investigation rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Economy or Soft Power (GM picks by job) marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Wyrdlens Adept or Cosmic Linguist. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Tier 1 — Gridbreakers

“Everything broken still remembers how it worked.”

Gridbreakers treat dead cities like sleeping machines. They know how to pry power from broken substations, wake lights in abandoned towers, and make a ruin choose sides. Where others see debris, they see leverage.

You’ve learned the first law of a dead city: if it still sparks, it still negotiates.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Investigation and the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic: In Ruins or Urban Wreckage hexes, salvage and material recovery are easier and more reliable.

Tier 1 — Prophet / Oracle

“You don’t know the future. You just know when something has started.”

At Tier 1, you begin catching the edge of events before they fully arrive. Not enough to command them. Enough to stop being surprised.

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank in Insight and Perception
  • 1/Soma Break, ask the GM one focused omen-question about an immediate situation, route, or known danger; the answer should be truthful but limited, symbolic, or pressure-based

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • Once per turn, before a planning-heavy, reconnaissance, or intrigue-forward action, gain +2 to one relevant OP roll by declaring what sign your Domain is acting on

Cost: early warning is rarely comfortable. Expect unease, distraction, or tension when you sense something going wrong before anyone else can justify reacting to it.
